capabilities.name: theme
capabilities.note: R2 treats image theme as a real support contract: PicoUI MAIN theme updates widget cache fields and the real LingDongGUI backend field `ldImage.maskColor` without disturbing bound image resources.

capabilities.name: style_class
capabilities.note: Style class is a stable widget-level metadata contract only. PicoUI and backend cache the pointer consistently, but image does not expose theme/style rendering parity.

capabilities.name: user_data
capabilities.note: Widget-level user_data is stably stored on both PicoUI and backend metadata paths. It is not a stronger visual or interaction parity claim.

capabilities.name: bg_text_border_radius_colors
capabilities.note: Image MAIN theme now synchronizes widget cache color/radius fields and uses the real backend `ldImage.maskColor` as the native-visible themed field.

capabilities.name: enabled
capabilities.note: Image enabled is no longer a reject boundary: PicoUI toggles widget enabled state and updates the real native ldBase selectable flag on the image backend.

widgets.audit_note: a-0.7 native-100 keeps image parity scoped to real ldImage public capabilities. Widget-level padding remains a generic PicoUI metadata/layout cache and is not counted as an ldImage native capability.

widgets.name: list

manual_artifact.note: This widget inherits final release manual evidence from the shared demo-level manual artifact catalog in docs/picoui-serial/C-线人工窗口验收记录.md.

capabilities.name: selected_index
capabilities.note: R4 closes list selected_index on a backend-truth-first contract, including the unselected -1 state. Native CLICKED_ITEM first synchronizes backend selection, then public/internal/cache state converge to the same index. Hidden or disabled lists release focus and rejected queued/native selection is rolled back to the current backend truth instead of leaving split-brain state. Repeated CLICKED_ITEM on the same index is a no-op and does not define a stronger confirm API.

capabilities.name: on_selected_callback_cookie
capabilities.note: callback cookie is intentionally separate from widget-level user_data

capabilities.name: item_marker
capabilities.note: R2 now treats list item marker as a real support contract: public selected_index setter/getter, backend value cache, and real LingDongGUI `ldList` selected marker stay synchronized in both setter-first and backend-truth readback paths.

capabilities.name: item_height
capabilities.note: R3B now exposes list item height as a real native contract: PicoUI setter writes straight through to the real LingDongGUI `ldList.itemHeight` field and invalid values are rejected without mutating backend truth.

capabilities.name: padding_margin
capabilities.note: R3B now exposes list padding and margin groups as real native contracts: PicoUI setters commit to the real LingDongGUI `ldList.padding` and `ldList.margin` fields, and invalid inputs are rejected without corrupting the last committed backend values.

capabilities.name: text_color
capabilities.note: R3B now exposes list text color as a direct native contract: PicoUI setter commits to real LingDongGUI `ldList.textColor` instead of only relying on theme-side style application.

capabilities.name: bg_color
capabilities.note: R3B now exposes list background color as a direct native contract: PicoUI setter commits to real LingDongGUI `ldList.bgColor` instead of only relying on theme-side style application.

capabilities.name: select_color
capabilities.note: R3B now exposes list select color as a direct native contract: PicoUI setter commits to real LingDongGUI `ldList.selectColor` instead of only relying on theme-side style application.

capabilities.name: align
capabilities.note: R3B now exposes list horizontal text alignment as a direct native contract: PicoUI accepts start/center/end and commits to real LingDongGUI `ldList.tAlign`, while unsupported spacing alignments are rejected.

capabilities.name: item_widget
capabilities.note: R3B now exposes list per-item widget as a real native contract: PicoUI reparents an existing backend child from the window tree into the real LingDongGUI `ldList` tree, then commits placement through `ldListSetItemWidget` instead of keeping a fake host-side pointer.

capabilities.name: style_class
capabilities.note: List style_class is a stable widget-level metadata contract. It is intentionally separate from any stronger item-level renderer identity.

capabilities.name: widget_level_user_data
capabilities.note: Widget-level user_data is stably stored on widget/backend metadata and remains distinct from on_selected callback cookies.

widgets.audit_note: a-0.7 native-100 records this widget as full_parity_complete: all required LingDongGUI public native capabilities in scope are covered by PicoUI public API, backend truth, and gate evidence.

capabilities.name: multi_button_and_indexed_callback
capabilities.note: PicoUI now exposes real multi-button strings, indexed callback bridge, and backend clickNum propagation against ldMessageBox.

capabilities.name: string_button_background_colors
capabilities.note: String colors, button release/press colors, and background color now map to real ldMessageBox fields.

capabilities.name: host_cached_readback_only
capabilities.note: Title/message/confirm text getters now reflect the same stable strings held by the real ldMessageBox backend path. Getter surface is still limited to title/message/final confirm text and does not expose full button catalog readback.

capabilities.name: multi_button_and_modal_behavior
capabilities.note: Multi-button strings and indexed callback are public support, and modal behavior is now proved as real topmost-hit capture plus dismiss-after-button-release against the LingDongGUI scene tree.

capabilities.name: modal_behavior
capabilities.note: LingDongGUI has no standalone isModal flag. The committed modal contract is overlap hit capture by the topmost ldMessageBox and real depose after button release, after which the underlay widget receives the next hit.

widgets.audit_note: R6B closes message_box with real multi-button strings, indexed callback bridge, topmost-hit modal behavior proof, and dedicated runtime/mapping/visible evidence.
